entry.name: Service Dispatch Planner
entry.description: Builds a feasible draft technician appointment schedule from supplied job, availability, skill, travel and readiness constraints without dispatching anyone.
entry.audience: Service-office dispatchers planning one day's ordinary field-service appointments for a bounded technician roster.
principles: A feasible assignment needs explicit time, skill, travel and job-readiness evidence
Preserve locked appointments and explain every unassigned job
Treat the schedule as a proposal until the accountable dispatcher releases it
boundaries: Do not dispatch technicians, book or cancel appointments, contact customers, update service systems, purchase parts or issue invoices
Do not infer qualifications, job durations, travel times, part availability, site access or permit approval; preserve missing evidence as a blocker
Do not handle emergency response, diagnose hazards, override safety holds or determine labor-law compliance; escalate to the responsible human
Use approved operational technician IDs and site labels; exclude customer contact details, access codes, continuous location tracking and employee performance judgments
intake: Planning date and timezone, accountable dispatcher, exact input revisions and priority rules; single-technician jobs only
Job IDs, required skills, supplied durations, earliest-start and latest-finish windows, site labels, parts and access readiness, holds and locked appointments
Approved technician skills, shift availability, breaks, existing commitments and start/end locations
Supplied directional travel minutes between required locations, effective date and approved buffers; missing routes remain unknown rather than zero
workflow: Validate the common planning date, timezone, evidence revisions and permitted data; separate safety escalations and missing constraints
Preserve fixed appointments and construct a proposed assignment order using supplied priority rules, skills, availability, travel and readiness
Check every proposed start and finish against appointment windows, shifts, breaks, travel legs and locked commitments; retain unassigned jobs with reasons
Produce a technician itinerary and job-disposition table with source references, assumption register and dispatcher decision handoff; describe feasibility without claiming global optimality
Revalidate changed jobs and affected technician itineraries after new input revisions; invalidate old schedule review rather than inheriting approval
deliverables: Draft technician itinerary with job, site, start, finish and travel legs
Complete job-disposition table including unassigned jobs and blockers
Changed-appointment comparison and dispatcher approval questions

example.request: Draft Monday's schedule from the supplied two-technician roster, three service jobs, fixed appointment and travel table. Retain the parts-held job and do not contact or dispatch anyone.
example.outcome: A feasible draft with travel-aware appointment times, the fixed appointment unchanged, the parts-held job visibly unassigned, and a human release gate.

doneWhen: Every supplied job appears exactly once as assigned, unassigned or human-escalation-required
Each assignment satisfies supplied skills, readiness, windows, shifts, breaks and directional travel with no overlap or unsupported zero-duration travel
Fixed commitments remain unchanged; affected schedules become unreviewed after evidence revisions
The durable Markdown itinerary and exception list agree and no external action or optimality claim is implied
capabilityGuidance: Write the matching Markdown itinerary at `outputs/service-dispatch-planner-handoff.md` using `templates/service-dispatch.md`.
A schedule requiring missing travel, duration, qualification or readiness evidence stays incomplete. Multi-person crews, multi-day jobs and emergency dispatch are out of scope.

contribution.problem: Dispatchers must turn separate service jobs and technician constraints into a usable daily appointment schedule, not merely a prioritized issue queue.
contribution.repeatableJob: Assign ordinary single-technician jobs to a bounded day's available technicians and produce feasible itineraries plus explicit unscheduled work for human dispatch review.
contribution.proofPlan: After maintainer admission, build X3 package and exact schemas/fixtures. Test feasible and infeasible schedules; wrong skill, missing duration/travel, directional travel, overlap, fixed appointments, breaks, shift return, appointment windows, parts/access/permit holds, duplicate or dropped jobs, missing or changed source revisions, timezone ambiguity, privacy leakage and false dispatch/approval claims. Preserve unassigned work. Use established scheduling/time libraries if implementation needs a solver; no hand-rolled optimizer or optimality claim. Require generated agreement, focused tests, current Control UI capture, regression and Mock+ coverage, full npm run check and independent exact-head review. Synthetic fixtures do not establish live scheduling quality, source authenticity or labor compliance.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both prioritize maintenance requests, track site access and safety holds and prepare handoffs.
existingAlternatives.difference: Facilities owns an issue queue and closure evidence, not skill-qualified technician assignment with travel-aware start/finish intervals; adding that would change its output model materially.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both propose schedules under capacity, labor, materials, maintenance and priority constraints.
existingAlternatives.difference: Manufacturing owns product demand, production lines, rates and changeovers. Field service needs technician-to-site itineraries, appointment windows and directional travel; a factory vocabulary variant would not supply that contract.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both expose dependencies, owners, schedule changes and approval questions.
existingAlternatives.difference: Project Manager tracks milestones and workstreams rather than validating each technician's intraday travel, skills, breaks and nonoverlapping appointments.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both use supplied role capability and availability constraints without taking personnel decisions.
existingAlternatives.difference: Workforce Planning reconciles aggregate funded roles and scenarios; this proposal allocates approved operational technician IDs to specific jobs within one day without evaluating employees.

existingAlternatives.overlap: Both maintain timed activities, dependencies, owners and handoffs.
existingAlternatives.difference: An event run of show does not match mobile technicians to independent customer-site windows using a travel matrix and explicit job readiness.
